newsitem.title: USA: Amerus to acquire Delta Life for $186 mln.
newsitem.headline: Amerus to acquire Delta Life for $186 mln.

text.p: AmerUs Life Holdings Inc said Thursday it had agreed to acquire Delta Life Corp of Memphis, Tenn., for $163 million cash plus assumption of about $23 million of debt.

Delta's major operating subsidiary is Delta Life and Annuity Co, with about $2.0 billion in assets. It provides single-premium deferred annuity and equity-indexed annuity products through a network of 4,000 producers. The company had total direct annuity deposits of $281 million in 1996.

"This acquisition gives us a bigger stake in the rapidly growing asset accumulation business. Also, we gain economies of scale and significantly expand our distribution network," said Roger Brooks, chairman, president and chief executive officer of AmerUs Life Holdings, parent of AmerUs Life Insurance Co.

Other than one-time transactional costs, the acquisition will have a slightly dilutive impact on AmerUs earnings this year, but company officials said they expect it will enhance earnings in 1998 and thereafter.
The transaction, which is expected to close before year-end, requires regulatory approval.
The acquisition will increase the total assets of AmerUs Life Holdings to $6.5 billion.

AmerUs said it intends to operate Delta Life as a separate company but plans to combine and consolidate most administrative functions in Des Moines by the end of the first quarter of 1998, in order to achieve significant expense reductions and operational efficiencies.
AmerUs Life Holdings was formed by the reorganization of American Mutual Life Insurance C. It serves about 320,000 customers with 424,000 life insurance policies and annuity contracts.
